nodes.name: Broadcast Trigger
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/broadcast. Body shape: {branch_slug, sender_profile, audience_segment, channels[], message_template, is_urgent, requested_by}. Called by admin-gui/server.js, never directly from the browser.

nodes.name: Fetch Sender Profile
nodes.notes: Runs once (single input item) before the member fetch, so its output is safely available to every later node via $('Fetch Sender Profile').first().json, including inside the Batch Members loop.

parameters.query:
SELECT sp.id AS sender_profile_id, sp.display_name, sp.signature_block, sp.contact_phone, sp.contact_email, b.id AS branch_id, b.sms_sender_id
FROM sender_profiles sp
JOIN branches b ON b.id = sp.branch_id
WHERE b.slug = $1 AND sp.role = $2 AND sp.is_active = true;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$json.branch_id, $json.sender_profile_id, $('Validate & Normalize Input').first().json.audience_segment, $('Validate & Normalize Input').first().json.channels, $('Validate & Normalize Input').first().json.message_template, $('Validate & Normalize Input').first().json.is_urgent, $('Validate & Normalize Input').first().json.requested_by] }}

nodes.name: Data Source Router
nodes.notes: DATA_SOURCE env var controls Phase 1 (sheets) vs Phase 2+ (postgres). Postgres is the path tested in this repo; sheets requires a live Google OAuth2 credential and is unverified.

parameters.query:
SELECT m.id AS member_id, m.first_name, m.last_name, m.email, m.phone_number,
       m.financial_status, m.committee_role, m.amount_due, m.branch_id
FROM members m
JOIN branches b ON b.id = m.branch_id
WHERE b.slug = $1 AND m.is_active = true;

nodes.name: Fetch Members (Sheets)
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: no live Google account was available to test this node. Column mapping assumes the Phase-1 sheet header row exactly matches docs/samples/nba_members_template.csv (First_Name, Last_Name, Email, Phone_Number, Financial_Status). Configure documentId/sheetName and the Google Sheets OAuth2 credential after import, then re-verify field names against a real spreadsheet.

nodes.name: Batch Members
nodes.notes: Output 0 (done) fires once after every batch has looped through; output 1 (loop) fires per batch and feeds the per-member send pipeline, which loops back into this node's input via the Wait node.

nodes.name: Select SMS Route
nodes.notes: is_urgent (legal/emergency notices) sets Multitexter's forcednd=1 to bypass Nigerian DND opt-outs for urgent legal/emergency notices; forcednd=0 otherwise. Confirmed against Multitexter's public API docs (https://www.multitexter.com/developers).

nodes.name: Send via Brevo Email
nodes.notes: Endpoint and body shape confirmed against Brevo's public API reference (developers.brevo.com/reference/sendtransacemail). Auth header is 'api-key', not Bearer.

nodes.name: Send via Brevo WhatsApp
nodes.notes: Endpoint/body base shape confirmed against developers.brevo.com/reference/sendwhatsappmessage AND against a real test call on 2026-08-08: contactNumbers must be an array of STRINGS (not numbers — the docs' bare-number example is misleading, confirmed by trial: a numeric value gets 'Invalid contactNumbers', a string value passes validation), without a leading '+'. Reached as far as 'senderNumber is invalid' with a placeholder sender, which requires a real WhatsApp number connected in Brevo's dashboard to get further. UNVERIFIED: Brevo's docs don't detail how per-message template parameters (e.g. {First_Name}) are passed on this endpoint — 'params' below is a best guess pending a real send with an approved template; check the response/Brevo dashboard and adjust if params aren't substituted. Interactive RSVP/payment buttons still require a Meta-approved WhatsApp template regardless of provider (BREVO_WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_ID is a placeholder until one is approved in the Brevo dashboard).

nodes.name: Send via Multitexter SMS
nodes.notes: Endpoint and body shape confirmed against multitexter.com/developers. Multitexter authenticates with account email+password IN the JSON body (no header/token auth), so this node uses authentication: none and reads MULTITEXTER_EMAIL/MULTITEXTER_PASSWORD from env instead of an n8n credential. recipients takes numbers WITHOUT a leading '+', comma-separated (a single number here since we send one member at a time).

nodes.name: Normalize Delivery Response (Email)
nodes.notes: Brevo returns HTTP 201 with a top-level messageId on success (confirmed in their API reference); on failure it returns an error body with no messageId. n8n's HTTP Request node surfaces the parsed body here regardless of status code (errors aren't thrown by default), so presence of messageId is the success signal.

nodes.name: Normalize Delivery Response (WhatsApp)
nodes.notes: Same messageId success signal as the email node, per Brevo's API reference. Still UNVERIFIED end-to-end since a real send needs an approved WhatsApp template — see notes on the Send via Brevo WhatsApp node.

nodes.name: Normalize Delivery Response (SMS)
nodes.notes: Response shape confirmed against a real send on 2026-08-08: {status: 1, msgid, units, balance, msg, messages: {"<phone-without-plus>": "<per-recipient-message-id>"}}. status is a NUMBER (1 = success); a failure shape wasn't observed (no failed send captured), so the ok-check falls back to treating any non-1 status as failure. If you hit a real failure response, capture it and tighten this further.

nodes.name: Insert Message Log
nodes.notes: Runs once per input item, i.e. once per (member, channel) pair — exactly the message_log grain.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO message_log (broadcast_id, member_id, branch_id, channel, recipient_address, status, provider_message_id, error_detail, sent_at)
VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, CASE WHEN $6 = 'sent' THEN now() ELSE NULL END);

nodes.name: Wait
nodes.notes: Throttles batch-to-batch pacing against Brevo/Multitexter rate limits before looping back to Batch Members.

parameters.query: UPDATE broadcasts SET status = 'completed', completed_at = now() WHERE id = $1::uuid;
